title: Maximum residue levels for maleic hydrazide
summary: EU proposes to increase MRLs for maleic hydrazide on animal products
update: The European Union (EU) proposes to increase the maximum residue levels (MRLs) for maleic hydrazide on a wide range of animal products.
impacted_products: Products of animal origin (swine, cattle, sheep, goat, horse, and poultry), milk, birds’ eggs
what_changing: The EU proposes to increase the MRLs for maleic hydrazide on most animal products (see Table 1).
why: Following an application for a change of MRLs by the producer of maleic hydrazide, the European Food Safety Authority evaluated the requested change and concluded that increasing the MRL would not pose a risk for consumers ( EFSA 2025 ).
timeline: The Regulation is expected to be published in October 2026, and will apply 6 months after publication.
background: MRLs are set in accordance with the rules set out in Regulation 396/2005 . For information on current MRLs for other substances, please consult the EU Pesticide Residues database . For further information on the setting of import tolerances, see Pesticide residue import tolerance MRLs explained .
resources: EFSA (2025) Peer review of the pesticide risk assessment of the active substance maleic hydrazide . EFSA Journal, 23(7): e9522.
